dek: Twelve Yosemite waterfalls with walk lengths, fees and the best time to go. Snowmelt peaks in May; Bridalveil and Vernal Fall are the easiest to plan around.
overview: Yosemite National Park, first protected in 1864, covers nearly 1,200 square miles of California and is best known for its waterfalls. The park's own description says the show is strongest in spring, when most of the snowmelt happens.

We cover twelve Yosemite waterfalls, and they are not all in the valley. Bridalveil Fall, Yosemite Falls, Vernal Fall and Nevada Fall are on the Merced River side of Yosemite Valley. Chilnualna Fall is near Wawona, Wapama Falls and Tueeulala Falls are at Hetch Hetchy, Le Conte Falls is on the Tuolumne River, and Pywiack Cascade is on Tenaya Creek.
fallsIntro: Bridalveil Fall and Vernal Fall have the most visitor reviews and the most complete trail details, so they are the easiest places to start. Yosemite Falls and Chilnualna Fall are longer hikes, and the rest have no published walk length in our files.
plan: For an easy valley day, pair Bridalveil Fall (0.5 mile round trip, about 80 feet of climbing) with Vernal Fall (2.4 miles round trip, about 1,000 feet up to the top on granite stairs). They start from different trailheads. Nevada Fall is the continuation past Vernal on the same route, according to the park's Vernal and Nevada page, though we don't have a separate mileage for it.

A second day could be the Yosemite Falls trail, 3.2 miles one way. Chilnualna Fall at Wawona is a longer hike at 3.9 miles one way and doesn't fit with the valley falls. Wapama Falls and Tueeulala Falls are in the Hetch Hetchy area, which has its own entrance station listed on the park's fee page.
flow: The USGS gauge on the Merced River at Happy Isles (11264500) is less than a mile from Vernal Fall. From 2019 through 2024 its average daily flow peaked in May at about 1,376 cubic feet per second and dropped to about 36 in September. That matches the park's own advice that spring snowmelt is the best waterfall season.
The gauge measures the Merced in the valley, so it tells you about Vernal Fall, Nevada Fall and the valley falls rather than Chilnualna Creek or Hetch Hetchy.
feesLead: Yosemite adds a separate per-person charge for visitors who are not US residents, and the park said in February 2026 that it will not use a timed reservation system this year.
access: In-person passes are sold at the South Entrance, Arch Rock, Big Oak Flat, Hetch Hetchy and Tioga stations, which take credit and debit cards only. The park suggests buying your pass before you arrive to skip the line, but it is not required.
safety: Vernal Fall is the hike with a posted warning. The park rates the Mist Trail moderate to strenuous, with steep granite stairs that get wet and slippery in high spray, and winter ice can close the stairs or make them hazardous. Bridalveil Fall is a much gentler half-mile walk rated easy, so don't judge one by the other.
